request: Where in the code is the rate limit applied, what are the default limit and window, and what does a client that goes over it get back?

oracle.answer: The limiter is rateLimit() in src/ratelimit.js: a fixed window per client address. createApp in src/app.js calls it before any route, using the limit and windowMs from src/config.js, whose defaults are 60 requests per windowMs of 60000 (one minute). # smoke-api

A tiny items API with no dependencies. Run it with `npm start`, test it with `npm test`.

## Endpoints

- `GET /health` returns `{ "ok": true, "service": "<name>" }`.
- `GET /items?page=1&limit=10` lists items, newest last. Pages start at 1. `limit` is at most 100.
- `GET /items/:id` returns one item.
- `POST /items` with `{ "name": "...", "price": 1.5 }` creates an item and answers 201.
- `DELETE /items/:id` removes an item and answers 204.

Every client is rate limited (see `src/ratelimit.js`).

## Configuration

Settings come from `src/config.js` (the defaults) and, when there is one, `config/local.json`, which is laid over them.

| Option | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `port` | The port the server listens on. | `3000` |
| `serviceName` | The name `/health` reports. | `smoke-api` |
| `limit` | Requests one client may make in a window. | `60` |
| `windowMs` | The length of the rate limit window, in milliseconds. | `60000` |
| `apiKey` | The key for the upstream service. Keep it in `config/local.json` or the environment, never in the README. | `<your api key>` |
